counterevidence_considered.description: The source_woodlot column groups colonies by collection site but, per the data description, is background information that does not make any row a repeat of another; the report treats woodlot tallies as descriptive only and applies no test to them.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: Woodlot is a grouping label, not a repeated-measures indicator; woodlot tallies are untested

source_refs.quoted_text:
Every colony was tested a single time, so the file holds no repeated measurements of
the same colony: the 20 rows are 20 independent observations, one per colony. The
woodlot label is background information about where a colony came from and does not
turn any row into a repeat of another row.

Woodlot tallies are descriptive; they are not tested. The single test above
uses one observation per colony, which is the independent unit of this study.

counterevidence_considered.description: The reported statistics were independently recomputed from the raw data and match: 15 of 20 colonies chose the narrow cavity (proportion 0.75), and the exact two-sided binomial p-value against p = 0.5 is 0.041389, confirming the test consumed each of the 20 independent rows exactly once with no inflated trial count.

evidence.description: The data description names colony_id as the independent-unit column and defines one row as one colony assayed once, so the issue class would require some colony_id to contribute more than one row to the binomial test.
evidence.observed_value: Independent unit column: colony_id; one row = one colony assayed once

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one field-collected ant colony, assayed once in the two-cavity choice arena
Independent unit column: colony_id
One trial is: one row

evidence.description: The row-independent procedure applied is an exact binomial test computed over all data rows (n_rows), so each row entering it is one trial; repeated rows for the same colony would inflate the trial count.
evidence.observed_value: binomtest(successes, n_rows, 0.5, two-sided) over all 20 rows

    result = binomtest(successes, n_rows, NULL_P, alternative="two-sided")

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by searching for any path through which one colony could enter the binomial test more than once: (1) scanned all 20 CSV rows for duplicate colony_id values and found none (TMN-01 through TMN-20 each appear exactly once); (2) checked whether the test's trial count (n_rows = 20) could exceed the number of distinct independent units and found n_rows equals the distinct colony_id count of 20; (3) checked whether the per-woodlot tallies are re-fed into any inferential procedure that would double-count colonies and found they are only formatted into a descriptive table with no test applied; (4) verified the workflow's uniqueness guard would abort execution on any repeated colony_id, so the produced report could not have been generated from data with repeated units. Every attempt to establish repeated independent-unit entry failed.
